diagnosis.hypothesis: The alert's symptom is real: POST /payments returns 503 because payments-api's provider circuit breaker (PROVIDER_BREAKER=on) is open and rejects calls to the provider without sending them. The breaker opened after the provider answered a small share of /v1/payments calls with HTTP 500 (about 0.1-0.24/s, against 1-3/s of 200s). While it is open or half-open with its single trial call out, nearly every payment is left pending and answered 503. The 4.1 s p95 on POST /payments is not explained by the provider's own latency, which stayed under 20 ms; I did not find where the time goes. The root cause of the provider's 500s is not established. I found no provider error traces, and I did not read the provider's error bodies. The breaker is the mechanism of the outage, not the cause. No deploy singles out a service: every container was recreated together at 06:06:34, about 2 minutes before the 503s began, so a restart of the whole stack is a candidate trigger, but I cannot confirm it.

evidence.shows: POST /payments 503s rose from about 0.04/s to 3.6/s at 06:08:21 and 9.6/s at 06:08:51, while 201s fell to 0.18/s. This confirms the alert.

All containers, including payments-api and fake-provider, were created at 06:06:34 with the same image. No single service's deploy stands out, and none has a setting that obviously explains the 500s. payments-api has PROVIDER_BREAKER=on.
payments-api errors say 'provider unavailable; payment left pending' because the circuit breaker is open, with the next trial call in about 6-7 s. Payments are rejected locally.
Calls to the provider were mostly 200, with some 500s at about 0.1-0.24/s from 06:07:18 until the calls stopped around 06:08:58. This is consistent with the breaker opening on provider 500s.
At 06:09:01 the breaker went half-open with one trial call, and other requests were refused because the trial call was still out.
Tempo holds no error traces for fake-provider, so the provider's 500s are not explained by what I could see.
The p95 of client calls to the provider stayed under 20 ms, so the provider was not slow. The 4.1 s p95 on POST /payments is unexplained.

proposed_fix.summary: No listed action fits. A rollback would restore settings from before the 06:06:34 recreation, but I found no bad setting, and the 500s may come from the provider. First find out why fake-provider answers /v1/payments with 500 (read the response bodies and its health). The breaker should close by itself once a trial call succeeds. Afterwards, run money_check to see whether the payments left pending were booked consistently with the provider's records.

diagnosis.blast_radius: No change is proposed, so nothing is affected. Payments stay pending or are refused with 503 while the breaker is open. A rollback of payments-api would pause it while it restarts and would not repair anything already booked.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Not applicable: no change is proposed.
